title: QUIC RFC 9000 S9P6P1 Preferred Address Conveyance And Per-Family Selection
purpose: Describe the focused S9P6P1 closure for preferred_address TLS conveyance and per-family preferred-address selection.
design_summary: Server preferred_address conveyance is proven through the deterministic TLS EncryptedExtensions transport-parameters message path, and per-family preferred-address behavior is proven through focused server encoding/client parsing and client family-selection tests.
data_and_state_considerations: The preferred_address transport parameter remains the single carrier for IPv4 and IPv6 preferred addresses, ports, preferred connection ID, and stateless reset token. Client-side selection continues to choose the preferred address family matching the original server path family after handshake confirmation.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The server-side preferred_address is carried inside the QUIC transport-parameters TLS extension in EncryptedExtensions.
Both IPv4 and IPv6 preferred-address families are preserved through server encoding and client parsing.
The client selects the IPv4 preferred address for an IPv4 original server path.
The client selects the IPv6 preferred address for an IPv6 original server path.
risks: This slice does not add public preferred-address configuration APIs.
This slice does not claim hosted interop readiness.
This slice does not close deferred fuzz obligations for S9P6P1.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the remaining generated S9P6P1 non-clean tail only: REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S9P6P1-0001, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S9P6P1-0006, and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S9P6P1-0007. It does not claim public migration APIs, multipath support, hosted interop readiness, or closure of deferred fuzz obligations.
